interactions.summary: Jiang closes by saying rereading reveals Dante's meaning, that Divine Comedy becomes a portal into the mind of God, and that a great book permanently changes the reader.

speaker_notes.note: Single-speaker closeout from Jiang; the only uncertainty is ASR noise in the opening clause.

claims.claim: On a first reading of Divine Comedy the reader cannot yet figure out what Dante saw, but repeated reading gradually reveals the work's secrets.
claims.temporal_scope: 2026-05-27 lecture claim about the reader's sequence of understanding

claims.claim: Once the reader understands what Dante saw, the reader can see the universe in the same way Dante saw it.
Jiang defines Divine Comedy first and foremost as a portal into the mind of God and uses that as his working definition of what a great book is.
Jiang predicts that Divine Comedy will change who the reader is forever.
claims.temporal_scope: future effect on readers as asserted on 2026-05-27

signature_moments.moment: The poem is not merely interpreted; it becomes a portal into the mind of God.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Divine Comedy is first and foremost a portal into the mind of God
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's climactic compression of the lecture's whole metaphysical reading and his strongest reusable phrase in the segment.

signature_moments.moment: A great book is defined by its power to alter the reader permanently.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it will change who you are forever
signature_moments.why_it_matters: Jiang ends by tying literary greatness to existential transformation rather than information or doctrine.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: A work that functions as a portal into the mind of God and transforms the reader through rereading.

glossary_terms.term: portal into the mind of God
glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's culminating description of what Divine Comedy is and what genuinely great literature does.

chronology_notes.note: Jiang makes the order of reading explicit: the first reading leaves the reader unable to understand, and later readings progressively uncover the work's meaning.

uncertainty_notes.note: The opening words are ASR-noisy ('how you see what what would it like comedy'), but the segment's core claim about rereading and revelation is still clear.
